Discussed tagging strategy, SSO and KMS concerns, and next-step pilot with a 2-week run to validate attribution. SE to do follow-up deep-dive on routing policies and caching impact on cost.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We also have Priya who will run the demo. Can folks intro?
[00:06] Evan Cruz: Hey Jordan, Evan here. FinOps for Grandview, been trying to get better cost split between product teams.
[00:10] Maya Lin: Maya, platform eng. Interested in how we map calls to our microservices and how to attach tags.
[00:14] Samir Patel: Samir, CTO. Mainly here to see whether we can get predictable economics and easy exports for our chargeback process.
[00:18] Rosa Nguyen: Rosa, security — will ask a few compliance Qs later.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) console walkthrough — route analytics and per-route cost, 2) tag strategy and export, 3) security notes, 4) next steps. We'll go live in the Console in a moment.
[02:03] Priya Menon: (screen share) Alright starting on the main Usage Overview page. Top left is aggregate token consumption by model family, you can break that down by route. Note sometimes our transcriptions label models odd — e g 'Redwood-RLX' might show as RLX or r l x in some older exports.
[03:05] Evan Cruz: Can you filter to date range and just show calls for our prod cluster? We have heavy daily traffic spikes.
[03:22] Priya Menon: Yep, date picker here, set to last 30 days. Now select route filter, here's /nlp/summarize-prod and /chat-bot-route-legacy, you can pin routes. The time series shows requests per minute, p95 latency, and cost per minute — cost is broken into model compute, infra (dedicated pool amortized), and cache savings.
[04:47] Maya Lin: How are dedicated infra costs amortized? We want to attach reserved pool costs to routes if they are pinned.
[05:03] Priya Menon: Good Q. If you reserve capacity (Dedicated) and pin routes to that pool, the Console will allocate a % of the monthly reserved commitment to those pinned routes by throughput share. There's also an option to use usage-only attribution for burst or shared pools. We can show a mock allocation.
[06:18] Jordan Blake: Important for chargeback is that exports show both allocated infra cost and per-token compute so finance can split fixed vs variable.
[06:32] Evan Cruz: Exactly — we need to demonstrate that to our finance team.
[07:01] Priya Menon: Switching to Per-Route Dashboard for /nlp/summarize-prod. Top panel shows throughput, latency histogram, and request distribution across models and quantization profiles. The cost panel beneath has columns: model cost, infra alloc, caching credit, and net route cost. Note the caching credit is computed from KV/prefix cache hit rates we've observed.
[08:10] Priya Menon: (slightly garbled) sometimes the auto-detect for cache keys mislabels KV cache as K V cache in exports, not a functional issue but the CSV column name differs.
[08:55] Maya Lin: Can we tag requests by tenant id so we can produce chargeback per customer?
[09:05] Priya Menon: Yes, we support route-level tags and request-level metadata that map to a route via our SDK or API headers — we have examples in the playbook. You can also attach application-level labels in the Console mapping UI.
[09:44] Samir Patel: About sampling — if we have noisy routes with millions of calls, how do you keep costs down for telemetry?
[09:58] Priya Menon: Console uses configurable telemetry sampling and rollups; by default we aggregate metrics at 1m granularity and you can enable full-fidelity traces for a short retention window to troubleshoot spikes. That keeps observability cost down.
[11:12] Jordan Blake: Let's demo export. Priya, go ahead and show the CSV export including the allocation columns.
[11:20] Priya Menon: Export -> select per-route -> choose date range -> include tags -> export. Here's a sample CSV (link shared in chat: https://redwood.app/s/exports/grandview-sample.csv). The CSV has column names like route, timestamp, requests, model_tokens, model_cost_usd, infra_alloc_usd, cache_savings_usd, net_cost_usd, tags.
[12:05] Evan Cruz: Perfect, we can drop that into our billing pipeline. Does the export include model variant names and quantization level?
[12:18] Priya Menon: Yes model_variant and quant_level columns included; occasionally the variant string gets normalized which may change hyphens to underscores depending on the model onboarding script.
[13:02] Rosa Nguyen: On the security side — how does Redwood handle customer-managed keys? We need KMS/HSM and audit logs.
[13:22] Priya Menon: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS; for hosted customers we provide KMS integration options and can arrange HSM for dedicated. We also stream audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. I'll attach the SOC2 security pack after.
[14:10] Rosa Nguyen: Do you have SSO and RBAC? We need fine-grained roles for console actions.
[14:18] Priya Menon: Yes SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC roles (Viewer, Analyst, Admin, SRE). We can demonstrate permissions off a test org.
[15:06] Jordan Blake: Competitor question — Evan asked earlier about someone named Nimbus, how are we different?
[15:16] Evan Cruz: Yeah, NimbusAI pitched a 'single pane' but their attribution was very coarse.
[15:24] Jordan Blake: Redwood focuses on per-route economics with model-level breakdown — and the unified runtime means the numbers map to actual serving variants, so chargeback is closer to truth.
[16:11] Priya Menon: Quick pivot: Route grouping. If you want to group related routes (e g all chat endpoints for product A) you can create route groups and the Console will roll costs up with optional rules. This is handy for product-level chargeback.
[17:05] Maya Lin: Can groups follow regex or tag-based rules?
[17:12] Priya Menon: Both — regex matching or tag rules; tag-based is preferred for dynamic microservice topologies.
[18:22] Samir Patel: About caching: does the Console show estimated token savings from prefix cache? We saw caching behavior vary per model.
[18:36] Priya Menon: Yes, there's a cache-savings estimator. We display measured hit rate and estimated token reduction; the cost panel shows both model cost saved and cache resource overhead if you run a dedicated cache layer.
[19:44] Evan Cruz: If we enable auto-batching or change batching windows, can we simulate cost impact?
[19:54] Priya Menon: There's a small modeling tool in Optimize — you can change batch size, concurrency, and you get projected per-token latency and cost. We can run a quick example: increase batch size from 8 to 16 reduces model cost by ~12% on this workload but raises p95 latency from 120ms to 210ms.
[21:03] Maya Lin: That's very useful. For our SLO we need p95 < 200ms for interactive support — that tradeoff seems acceptable in some routes.
[21:18] Priya Menon: For interactive routes, you can pin to low-latency pool and keep batching low; for background routes we can push to higher batch sizes on cheaper hardware.
[22:05] Jordan Blake: Let's talk pilot. Evan — what's your success criteria?
[22:12] Evan Cruz: We want: 1) accurate per-route cost alignment to our billing, 2) CSV exports fit into our chargeback pipeline, 3) security signoff (SOC2 artifacts + KMS plan). If those check, we run a 2-week pilot against two routes: /nlp/summarize-prod and /chat-support.
[22:34] Priya Menon: That sounds good. We'll enable full-fidelity telemetry for the pilot and export daily snapshots.
[23:12] (crosstalk) Samir Patel: Did you say daily snapshots? Fine — but show us the latency impact of telemetry.
[23:28] Priya Menon: Telemetry is async, negligible impact on request latency. We can confirm with a baseline run.
[24:05] Jordan Blake: Quick Q from Maya: can we add custom cost buckets?
[24:12] Priya Menon: Yes you can define custom buckets (e g ML infra, support infra, third-party tokens) and map route costs into those buckets via UI rules or CSV-based mappings.
[25:30] Priya Menon: (typing) I'm also pulling up an example of a canary rollout: you can route a portion of traffic to a new model variant and the Console will show comparative cost & quality metrics side-by-side. Very handy to validate cheaper quantized variants.
[26:45] Maya Lin: Are quality regressions surfaced? We need eval hooks tied to prompt sets.
[26:55] Priya Menon: Yes Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set evals and flag regressions — we can tie alerts to your SLOs. We'll include an example alerting rule in the playbook.
[28:02] Evan Cruz: On the chargeback CSV, what about internal teams that share accounts? We need mapping table for team owners.
[28:18] Priya Menon: You can upload a mapping file or connect to your internal registry — we support a static mapping CSV and a dynamic API to resolve owner by tenant id.
[29:30] Jordan Blake: Let's field some compliance specifics for Rosa.
[29:37] Rosa Nguyen: Two Qs — data retention policies for logs, and ability to prove data isolation for Dedicated pools.
[29:44] Priya Menon: Logs retention configurable; for hosted we have default 90 days but can extend for paid tiers. Dedicated pools provide network isolation and private endpoints; we can provide network diagrams and architecture for your auditors.
[30:50] Rosa Nguyen: Great. Also want to review SAML attributes and SCIM mapping later.
[31:02] Priya Menon: We'll send a SAML/SCIM guide.
[31:36] (pause) Priya Menon: Now switching to a quick walkthrough of the Optimize cost modeler: here you can pick routes, change quantization, batch, and run a delta estimate. For this demo I toggled quantization to 8-bit and it shows ~30% model cost reduction at the expense of some eval delta.
[33:10] Maya Lin: Do you surface the eval delta numeric? Like a BLEU-like score?
[33:18] Priya Menon: We show a customizable metric — accuracy or semantic similarity — you upload prompt examples and we run comparisons, produce a delta % and examples where outputs diverge.
[34:25] Evan Cruz: For our finance team the net-cost delta is key. Can you include amortized license costs?
[34:33] Priya Menon: Yes you can add manual line-items to the model cost — e g per-month model license — and the Console includes those in net route cost.
[35:20] Jordan Blake: Side note — MIME types and request schema. Maya will take the SDK for a spin?
[35:28] Maya Lin: Yes I'll try the node SDK example you mentioned. The mapping code for tags looked straightforward.
[36:00] Priya Menon: Back to exports, here's the sample mapping template for chargeback (shared as link: https://redwood.app/s/playbooks/grandview-mapping). Links posted in chat.
[36:44] Evan Cruz: One of our concerns was vendor lock and model portability — if we change model provider can you remap old exports?
[36:55] Priya Menon: Exported data is model-agnostic; the Console references model IDs but we include model normalization rules. If you switch providers we can remap via a migration script.
[37:32] Samir Patel: Any throttles or rate limits we should be aware of when shipping high-throughput telemetry?
[37:42] Priya Menon: Telemetry ingestion supports high throughput; limit tiers exist for API usage but for pilot we'll provision accordingly.
[38:10] Jordan Blake: We're nearing the end. Recap of commitments: Jordan sends CSV + pricing; Priya sends playbook and SAML guide; schedule SE deep-dive.
[38:28] Priya Menon: Quick final Q for Evan: will you enable pinned routes to Dedicated for pilot or keep hosted?
[38:36] Evan Cruz: We'll start hosted to validate attribution, then move hot routes to Dedicated if economics look right.
[38:52] Priya Menon: Makes sense.
[39:10] Rosa Nguyen: One last note: please redact any PII in the shared exports.
[39:18] Priya Menon: Yep we'll strip PII by default and we can include a PII-scrubbed export option.
[40:05] Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Any final Qs?
[40:12] (silence)
[40:30] Evan Cruz: Nope that's it. Thanks Priya.
[40:35] Samir Patel: Thanks.
[40:40] Maya Lin: Thanks all.
[40:44] Jordan Blake: End call.
[51:55] (meeting auto-end marker)
